Elecom Launches a Handy USB-C Dock with Dial and Macro Keys

Posted by Bahleem | Oct 8, 2026

Table of Contents

Toggle
  • A compact design with built-in controls
  • Plenty of useful ports
    • Elecom DST-L080BPBK specifications
  • A useful idea for a crowded desk
  • Price and availability
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:55
Instaread

Elecom has introduced a new USB-C docking station that does more than just add extra ports to a laptop. The new DST-L080BPBK combines an 8-in-1 dock with a large control dial and four customizable buttons.

This makes the dock interesting for people who want quick access to shortcuts while also needing more connectivity. Instead of reaching for software controls every time, users can assign different actions to the dial and buttons.

The dock is designed for Windows 10, Windows 11, and macOS Tahoe 26. Elecom plans to release it in Japan in early October.

A compact design with built-in controls

The Elecom DST-L080BPBK measures 74 × 87 × 59 mm and weighs around 250 g. Its compact size should make it easy to keep beside a laptop, monitor, or desktop PC without taking up much desk space.

The main feature is located on the top. There is a large dial knob surrounded by four physical buttons. Elecom allows users to change their functions through its Mouse Assistant software.

The dial and buttons can be set up for different tasks depending on the user’s workflow. They could be useful for volume control, media playback, shortcuts, application commands, or other supported functions.

This is what separates the DST-L080BPBK from a normal USB-C hub. It works as a small desktop control panel as well as a docking station.

Plenty of useful ports

Despite its small body, the dock offers a good selection of connections.

For USB devices, it includes one USB Type-C port and two USB Type-A ports, all supporting 5 Gbps data speeds. There is also a USB Type-C upstream connection for linking the dock to a computer.

The USB-C Power Delivery port supports up to 100 W input and up to 90 W output. This means a compatible laptop can receive power through the dock while the other ports remain available for accessories.

For displays, there is one HDMI port with support for resolutions up to 4K at 60 Hz. This should be enough for a sharp external display for office work, browsing, and general desktop use.

The dock also includes SD and microSD card slots, making it useful for photographers, content creators, and anyone who regularly moves files from memory cards.

Other connections include Gigabit Ethernet for wired networking and a 3.5 mm audio jack.

Elecom DST-L080BPBK specifications

A useful idea for a crowded desk

The biggest selling point of the DST-L080BPBK is not simply the number of ports. USB-C docks with HDMI, Ethernet, card readers, and USB ports are already common.

The built-in dial and four macro keys are what make this model different.

For example, the dial could be used to control system volume while the four buttons handle mute, play/pause, opening an application, or other shortcuts. The exact functions will depend on what Elecom’s software supports.

This could be particularly useful for people who spend a lot of time at their desk. A physical control is often faster than opening an application or searching through menus.

Price and availability

Elecom plans to launch the DST-L080BPBK in Japan in early October. The company’s website lists the dock at ¥13,728, which is roughly $87.

There is currently no confirmed information about availability in other regions.
